meta.title: Two Readers, One Page
meta.skill_frame: Process: see why one check cannot replace a second check for a different fault.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 5.88, 5.46 and 6.00 on the three parts (110, 112 and 103 words), 5.73 together. Two readers, two defects, one page: the load is seeing that a clean pass for words says nothing about the columns.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for process 4.2, band 4.2, sequence 4. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A weekly newspaper page checked twice, once for words by a copy editor and once for space by a compositor.
source.avoided: No paper, town, or staff name. No claim about print volume, wages, or page size.

session.difficulty_basis: Two checks run on the same page and each is blind to the other's defect, so the reader must see why one pass cannot stand for both.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A weekly paper sets each page in metal type, then pulls a proof on paper. The proof goes first to the copy editor, who reads it the way a reader would. She looks for a wrong name, a missing word, or a sentence that says the opposite of what the reporter meant. Her marks sit in the margin beside the line. She does not look at the width of the columns or the edges of the advertisements. Her job is the words, and she reads every one of them on the page. A wrong name printed in a wedding notice reaches a thousand homes before the office can correct it.
passage.part_2: The same proof then goes to the compositor, who checks the page as a piece of work. He measures each column against the frame. A column that runs long pushes the last line off the page. He checks that the borders of the advertisements line up and that no headline sits over the wrong story. He lays a ruler along the frame and counts the lines in each column. The frame is measured in inches, and a page that fits it will print without a fold. He reads very little of the text. A wrong name means nothing to his ruler, and a column that overruns means nothing to the copy editor.
passage.part_3: Both reads happen before the press starts, and neither can replace the other. A page that passes the copy editor can still be crooked, and a page that passes the compositor can still name the wrong mayor. The page is set, read for words, read for space, and then printed. One reader could do both jobs, but not in one pass, because the two reads look for different defects. Skipping either read sends a page to the press that only half a crew has checked. The two reads are cheap next to a reprinted page, so the paper pays for both of them.

items.prompt: What does the copy editor look for as she reads?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. A wrong name, a missing word, or a sentence that says the opposite.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The first part names the three faults she looks for.
tutor_only.tell: She looks for a wrong name, a missing word, or a sentence that says the opposite of the report.
help: The sentence about her marks names the faults she looks for.
Two are small and one reverses the meaning.
tutor_only.core_idea: A wrong name, a missing word, or a sentence that says the opposite of what the reporter meant.
accept_ideas: wrong names, missing words, and sentences that say the opposite
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says she checks the column widths
if_they_say.ask: The passage says she does not look at the columns. What does she read for?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Each column against the frame.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says he measures each column against the frame and checks the advertisement borders.
tutor_only.tell: He measures each column against the frame. A column that runs long pushes the last line off.
help: The sentence about the frame names what he measures.
He compares the column with the frame.
tutor_only.core_idea: Each column against the frame, and the advertisement borders.
accept_ideas: the column width and the advertisement borders
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he measures the sentences
if_they_say.ask: He reads very little of the text. What does he hold the ruler against?

items.prompt: Why does the compositor read very little of the text?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. A wrong name means nothing to his ruler.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says he reads very little, because a wrong name means nothing to his ruler.
tutor_only.tell: His job is the space on the page. A wrong name does not change the measurement.
help: The sentence about his ruler says what the page is to him.
He is checking space, not meaning.
tutor_only.core_idea: His job is the space; a wrong name does not change any measurement.
accept_ideas: a wrong name does not affect the columns
measuring the page does not need reading
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he cannot read
if_they_say.ask: Reading is not the issue. What would a wrong name change on his ruler?

items.prompt: A page passes the copy editor and is still wrong. What could be wrong, and why did she miss it?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It could be crooked, and she never measures columns.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The third part says a page that passes the copy editor can still be crooked, because the two reads look for different defects.
tutor_only.tell: The page could be crooked or the borders could be off. She does not measure columns or borders.
help: The sentence about a crooked page names the fault she cannot see.
Her marks are in the margin beside the line, not on the frame.
tutor_only.core_idea: A column could run long or the advertisement borders could be off, because she does not measure the page.
accept_ideas: the columns or the advertisement borders could be wrong
the page could be laid out badly
its space is wrong because she checks words only
not_required: what she wrote in the margin
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the page could have a wrong name
if_they_say.ask: She reads every word, so a name would not reach her blind spot. What does she never measure?

items.prompt: Why can one reader not do both jobs in one pass?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The two reads look for different defects.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The third part says the two reads search for different defects, so neither replaces the other.
tutor_only.tell: The two reads look for different defects. Looking for words is not measuring columns.
help: The sentence about the two readings names what each one seeks.
Each reader is looking for a different kind of fault.
tutor_only.core_idea: The two reads look for different defects, so one pass cannot do both jobs.
accept_ideas: each read looks for a different fault
finding words does not find a crooked column
one reader can only look for one kind of error
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the job is too long for one person
if_they_say.ask: Time is not the reason given. What is each reader looking for?
